title: Common Architecture Language Model (CALM) Layout Vocab
description: A layout is a presentation-only sidecar document that records where the elements of a CALM document should be drawn. It carries no architectural meaning: removing every layout leaves the architecture it targets semantically unchanged.

for.description: Reference to the CALM document this layout applies to. Deliberately not version-qualified, so a single layout can float across versions of the target document.

name.description: Human-readable name for this layout, e.g. 'Default'.

pins.description: Fixed positions for elements of the target document, matched by unique-id. Elements of the target with no pin are positioned by the renderer's own automatic layout. A pin whose unique-id is no longer present in the target document is ignored rather than treated as an error, so a layout stays usable as the architecture evolves.

unique-id.description: The unique-id of the node, relationship or group in the target document that this pin positions.

x.description: Horizontal coordinate in the renderer's abstract layout space, not pixels.

y.description: Vertical coordinate in the renderer's abstract layout space, not pixels.
